props.title: Two Weeks Notice

sections.content: Two Weeks Notice (2002) stands as a quintessential early-2000s romantic comedy, showcasing Sandra Bullock and Hugh Grant at the height of their rom-com powers. The film follows the familiar but effective workplace romance formula established by hits like Working Girl (1988) and The Proposal (2009), but adds sharp commentary about corporate development versus historic preservation. Bullock's portrayal of dedicated lawyer Lucy Kelson brings the same endearing determination she perfected in Miss Congeniality (2000), while Grant continues his charming-but-clueless persona from Notting Hill (1999). Two Weeks Notice|2002|A dedicated environmental lawyer gives her millionaire boss two weeks notice and finds herself falling for him|HBO Max Sweet Home Alabama|2002|A fashion designer must confront her past and her first love when she returns home to finalize her divorce|Disney+ Laws of Attraction|2004|Two divorce lawyers find themselves falling in love while representing opposing clients|Prime Video

The film marked a significant moment in workplace romantic comedies, bridging the gap between the power-dynamic stories of the 1990s like Pretty Woman (1990) and the more equality-focused narratives that would follow in films like The Devil Wears Prada (2006). The chemistry between Bullock and Grant particularly shines in their verbal sparring, reminiscent of classic screwball comedies like His Girl Friday (1940), but updated for modern sensibilities.

Director Marc Lawrence's approach to the genre follows the successful template of other millennial-era romantic comedies like You've Got Mail (1998) and Bridget Jones's Diary (2001), where professional women navigate both career ambitions and romantic entanglements. The film's New York setting becomes almost a character itself, similar to how the city functions in When Harry Met Sally (1989). The Proposal|2009|A publishing executive forces her assistant to marry her to avoid deportation|Disney+ Set It Up|2018|Two overworked assistants try to set up their demanding bosses|Netflix 27 Dresses|2008|A perpetual bridesmaid finds herself falling for a cynical journalist|Hulu SUBHEAD: Evolution of the Corporate Romance

Two Weeks Notice helped establish a specific rom-com subgenre focused on corporate relationships that would influence later films like The Ugly Truth (2009) and Long Shot (2019). These films typically explore the tension between personal values and professional success, while maintaining the light touch necessary for romantic comedy success.
